title: Bern-Barcelona EEG database: focal and nonfocal intracranial EEG signal pairs (Andrzejak, Schindler & Rummel 2012)
description: The Bern-Barcelona EEG database provides 7500 pairs of intracranial EEG signals (3750 focal and 3750 non-focal) drawn from five patients with pharmacoresistant temporal lobe epilepsy. Each pair consists of two neighbouring channels, 20 s long, sampled at 512 Hz. This BIDS repackaging losslessly converts the published text files to BrainVision format. All runs are pooled under one pseudo-subject because patient, channel and time of origin were not stored.
methods_description: Intracranial strip and depth electrodes recorded long-term iEEG in five epilepsy surgery candidates at the University of Bern. The source data were band-pass filtered at 0.5-150 Hz (zero-phase Butterworth), down-sampled to 512 Hz where needed, and re-referenced to the median of artifact-free channels. Focal channels were those showing the first ictal changes, judged by at least two electroencephalographers. 20-s windows were randomly selected, excluding seizures and the following three hours, and pairs with prominent artifacts were discarded. Values were converted to float32 BrainVision files with no filtering, resampling or rescaling.
